messages:
maria: heads-up — seeing a sporadic p99 laddering on hosted API for /v1/generate (llm-7b-open). p95 ok (~220ms) but p99 jumped to ~1.8s in short waves starting 10:12 UTC. queue depth oscillating.
ryan: which pool/region? any tenant heatmap?
maria: pool: eu-west-2/gpu-pool-7b. tenants noisy: acme-inc shows bursty priming. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/shot/abcd (short link)
anika: @maria can you paste kernel-selector & batcher logs around 10:12?
maria: grabbing logs now, snippets below:
```text
[10:12:05] kernel-selector: choose=gpu_fast alt=gpu_aux reason=latency_budget_miss
[10:12:05] batcher: queued=42 batch_len=1 sampler=continuous underflow
[10:12:06] kvcache: evict=hot-prefix tenant=acme-inc rate=610/s
[10:12:07] kernel-selector: fallback-triggered model=llm-7b-open dest=gpu_aux
```
ryan: batch_len=1 + queued=42 suggests sampler is creating many tiny batches -> high scheduling overhead. could be continuous-batching underflow due to pacing.
anika: kvcache evict spike lines up. noisy priming probably flushing KV and causing cache misses, exacerbating latency.
sanjay: checking tenant: acme-inc ran a feed job at 10:10 that ramped concurrent sessions from 5 -> 180 over ~20s. sequence length variance high.
maria: queue backlog numbers: pool queue went 600 -> 2100 requests for ~40s. rate limiter didn't pre-throttle; tokens depleted and sampler fell back to immediate flush.
deploy-bot: rate-limiter-config v2 rolled to 50% of servers at 10:05 by rollout/canary-2026-03-18
anika: that rollout could've changed per-tenant pacing semantics and interacts poorly with continuous batching. rollouts + noisy tenant = sawtooth latency.
perf-bot: uploaded profile: flamegraph and CPU timeline for gpu-pool-7b at 10:12 -> https://artifacts.redwood/prof/fg-2423456789
ryan: propose quick mitigation: increase continuous_batch.max_batch_delay in canary from 12ms -> 40ms to allow coalescing, and pin kernel-selector to prefer gpu_fast for already-hot model variants.
maria: applied canary bump to 10% of the pool. p99 in canary dropped to ~600ms within 90s, still seeing laddering on non-canary shards.
sanjay: digging deeper — kernel-selector shows oscillation every ~15-30s where requests flip to gpu_aux for some shards. gpu_aux uses fallback kernels optimized for short contexts; long contexts cause token step cost spike.
anika: root causes = (1) noisy tenant priming -> kvcache thrash -> cache miss penalty, (2) rate-limiter rollout changed pacing -> sampler underflow, (3) kernel-selector oscillation sending long-context requests to suboptimal kernels.
ryan: immediate steps:
- revert rate-limiter rollout to old pacing on the affected canary group OR restrict v2 to non-prod pools
- add a temporary sticky affinity: kernel-selector.sticky_ttl=120s for tenant/model combos with >200qps
- add a reactive rule: if kvcache.eviction_rate > 500/s && batcher.batch_len < 2 then auto-bump batch_delay and increase cache target by +20%
maria: implemented sticky affinity in canary and added the kvcache reactive rule. monitoring now. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1234
perf-bot: post-mitigation snapshot: p99 down to ~340ms on canary, global p99 trending toward 520ms.
anika: long-term: need selector stability (avoid oscillation), better early throttling for noisy tenants, and sampler sensors that detect underflow before flushing. open a design ticket?
ryan: I'll own the sampler sensors RFC. will draft today.
maria: copied notes into incident doc and updated runbook: add checks for continuous_batch underflow + kvcache eviction spikes + kernel-selector fallbacks. linking incident doc: https://confluence.redwood/incident/2423456789
anika: nice work. monitor 30m and we'll decide if full rollback of rate-limiter v2 is needed. :eyes:
maria: thanks all — closing thread if metrics stay stable. :thumbsup:
